title: Clinical Mastery: Infective & Fungal Keratitis
summary: A comprehensive guide for the ophthalmic clinician addressing fungal keratitis presentation, diagnostics, and evidence-based management. This resource bridges clinical pearls with the latest trial data from the Mycotic Ulcer Treatment Trials.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation: The Fungal Index
sections.content: A 30-year-old presents to the clinic with complaints of decreased vision and mild pain in his right eye. He vaguely recalls being hit in the right eye with a tree branch while pruning his garden around 3 weeks back. He had mild discomfort in his eye since then and his vision has been gradually worsening. Clinical signs include: pale whitish paracentral infiltration involving the visual axis, fuzzy margins, and surrounding wispy satellite lesions. A pale whitish hypopyon filling approximately one-fifth of the Anterior Chamber. Severe conjunctival congestion. (Note: Fungal hypopyon typically features a convex upper border, low mobility with head posture, and yellow color, whereas bacterial hypopyon is concave, mobile, and whitish.)

rows: Vegetative trauma, fuzzy margins, satellite lesions, slow course.
Rapid onset, concave hypopyon, purulent discharge.
Pain out of proportion, ring infiltrate, neural involvement.

sections.title: Diagnostic Investigation Workup
content: Direct Microscopy: KOH preparation for rapid evaluation.
Staining: Gram, Giemsa, PAS, Calcofluor white, Methenamine Silver, ZN stain (if Mycobacterial suspected).
Culture Media: Blood agar (General), Chocolate agar (Fastidious), Sabouraud dextrose agar (Fungi), Non-nutrient agar with E. coli (Acanthamoeba).
Advanced: PCR analysis, Corneal biopsy, Anterior chamber tap, In vivo confocal microscopy (IVCM).

sections.title: Evidence-Based Studies (MUTT)
content: MUTT 1: Topical Natamycin 5% vs. Voriconazole 1%. Natamycin is superior for filamentous fungi.
MUTT 1: Fusarium Keratitis - Avoid Voriconazole monotherapy.
MUTT 2: Oral Voriconazole added to topical therapy showed no overall benefit, except potentially in Fusarium cases.

sections.title: Management & Pharmacology
sections.content: Medical management: Hospital admission for severe cases, topical antifungals (hourly), broad-spectrum antibiotics for co-infection, and cycloplegia. Antifungal classes: Polyenes (Amphotericin B, Natamycin - ergosterol complexing) and Azoles (Fluconazole, Voriconazole - CYP450 inhibition). Adjuncts: Doxycycline 100mg BID (anti-collagenase), Vitamin C. Surgical: Debridement of epithelium, Therapeutic PKP, Tissue glue, or Conjunctival flap. Note: Adjuvant cross-linking is not effective and potentially harmful.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Biopsy
content: Absence of clinical improvement after 3-4 days.
Deep stromal involvement with intact epithelium.
